name: Ischaemic Heart Disease and Myocardial Infarction

reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Necrosis wavefront moves subendocardium outward; time is muscle
Wall rupture risk peaks three to seven days post infarction
LAD infarction threatens anterior wall, septum and conduction
reference.pathophysiology: Occlusive thrombus on disrupted plaque starves downstream myocardium, depleting ATP until membrane failure and coagulative necrosis spread outward. Reperfusion restores oxygen but floods injured cells with calcium and reactive species. Healing replaces necrosis with collagen that cannot contract, predisposing to aneurysm, mural thrombus and arrhythmia.
additionalInvestigations: Serial troponin with ECG territory localisation
Echocardiography for mechanical complications and ejection fraction
Coronary angiography to define culprit anatomy
